detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) describes sleep apnea treatment as built around keeping the airway open during sleep, usually after a sleep study confirms the diagnosis. Positive airway pressure (PAP) machines are presented as the most common treatment: a continuous PAP (CPAP) machine provides constant air pressure through the mouth or nose, and other PAP types vary the pressure. NHLBI notes that PAP treatment is often paired with lifelong healthy lifestyle changes, which sources describe as regular physical activity, healthy sleep habits, reaching a healthy weight, limiting alcohol, and quitting smoking.

Other options in the sources include oral devices worn in the mouth to prevent a blocked airway, described for people who do not want to use or cannot tolerate a CPAP machine, exercises for the mouth and facial muscles called orofacial therapy, and, for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity, a weight-loss medicine class approved by the FDA. Surgical procedures are described in some cases, including hypoglossal nerve stimulation and weight-loss surgery when obesity contributes and other treatments do not work.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about sleep apnea treatment options.
sourceName: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
summary: NHLBI outlines sleep apnea treatment centered on positive airway pressure machines such as CPAP, paired with lifestyle changes, with oral devices, orofacial therapy, medicines, and surgery described for selected cases.
takeaways: pap machines such as cpap are the most common treatment
lifestyle changes are paired with device treatment
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Sleep apnea: keeping the airway open with PAP and other treatments
